title: How the Elephant Got His Trunk
blurb: A curious young elephant asks one question too many.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… the Elephant had no trunk at all. [surprised] He had only a blackish bulgy nose, as big as a boot, that he could wriggle from side to side — [playfully] but he could not pick anything up with it.

[curious] Now there was one Elephant, a NEW Elephant, a young one… and he was full of questions.

[excited] He asked his tall aunt the Ostrich why her tail feathers grew just so. He asked his tall uncle the Giraffe what made his skin so spotty. He asked his broad aunt the Hippopotamus why her eyes were red.

[amused] And every single time he asked a question… [short pause] every single one of them spanked him.

[curious] But he was still full of questions.

Then one fine morning he asked a brand new one. “What does the Crocodile have for dinner?”

[worried] And everybody said “Hush!” in a loud and dreadful tone, and spanked him again, for a long time.

[firmly] But the Elephant's Child still wanted to know. [excited] So he packed a hundred pounds of sugar-cane, and seventeen melons, and went off to find out for himself.

[softly] He went and he went, through the great grey-green greasy Limpopo River, all set about with fever trees.

[curious] And there on the bank he trod on what he thought was a log of wood. [surprised] But it was really the Crocodile — and the Crocodile winked one eye.

[excited] “Excuse me,” said the Elephant's Child politely, “but have you seen a Crocodile in these parts?”

[mischievously] “Come hither, little one,” said the Crocodile. “I AM the Crocodile.”

[excited] “You are the very person I have been looking for!” cried the Elephant's Child. “Will you please tell me what you have for dinner?”

[whispers] “Come hither, little one,” said the Crocodile, “and I shall whisper it.”

[curious] So the Elephant's Child put his head down close to the Crocodile's musky, tusky mouth. [surprised] And the Crocodile caught him by his little blackish bulgy nose.

[worried] “I think,” said the Crocodile, and he said it between his teeth, “I think today I shall begin with Elephant's Child.”

[loudly] Well, the Elephant's Child was much annoyed. He sat back on his little haunches and PULLED. [firmly] And the Crocodile pulled too.

[worried] And the Elephant's Child's nose began to stretch. [surprised] It grew longer. And longer. And LONGER.

[excited] At last the Crocodile let go with a splash, and the Elephant's Child sat down hard — [amused] with a nose five whole feet long.

[worried] At first he was very sorry about it. [thoughtful] But then he found he could pluck grass with it. [playfully] He could pick up a melon. He could throw cool mud upon his head. [amused] And when a fly bit him, he could brush it away.

[warmly] So he went home again. [amused] And within a week, every single elephant who had ever spanked him had gone down to the great grey-green greasy Limpopo… to get a new nose of their own.
